title: ChatGPT points to a blood pressure medication behind an 18-month cough that doctors had not explained; a doctor confirms it and changes the prescription, and X user Shreya's mother may be healing
summary: ChatGPT flagged a BP drug side effect behind an 18-month cough; a doctor confirmed it and changed the drug; daughter reports mother healing.
account: On 23 July 2025 an X user posting as Shreya.tsx (@Life_of_coder, profile location “india”) wrote about her mother. Her mother had had a nonstop cough for 1.5 years. That was despite top doctors, big hospitals in and outside their city, homeopathy, ayurveda and allopathy. Internal bleeding had begun. Doctors had warned the condition could be fatal within six months. She described everything to OpenAI's ChatGPT, which listed possible causes including blood pressure medication. It asked whether the prescription contained a specific ingredient. It did. A doctor, told of this, confirmed it at once and changed the medication. Her mother was “finally healing”. Four Indian outlets reported the post on 24 July 2025. It has since been deleted.
purpose: ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose conversational assistant, not a diagnostic or drug-safety tool. Surfacing a medication side effect as the likely cause of a chronic cough was outside what it was built for. So the benefit is marked unexpected.
segment: Consumer use by a patient's adult daughter

ratings.reason: One identifiable patient, the poster's mother, had an 18-month cough with internal bleeding that doctors had warned could become fatal. After the medication change her daughter reported her “finally healing”. Material for one person. It rates below life-changing because the recovery was in progress. Nothing beyond the daughter's post documents the diagnosis or the outcome.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT generated the hypothesis. Among several possible causes it listed blood pressure medication. When told the mother was on such medication, it asked whether the prescription contained a specific ingredient, which it did. The confirmation and the prescription change were made by a doctor (“He confirmed it instantly and changed the meds”). NDTV, Mint, Mashable India and the Financial Express quote a commenter. They say cough is a known side effect of BP medicine that doctors “should've checked”. That frames the contribution as surfacing a documented side effect rather than a novel diagnosis. No clinician comments on the chatbot's role. The whole sequence rests on the daughter's account.
